requirements.requirement: Ordinary nested archive members are unpacked under incoming/.
requirements.summary: normal.tar successfully created incoming/docs/notice.txt with the expected content; the behavior and installed data remained valid after restart.

requirements.requirement: Archives containing absolute paths are rejected before installing members or writing outside incoming/.
requirements.summary: absolute.tar was rejected with exit 1, /outside.txt was absent, incoming/ had not been created, and relevant source/protected hashes remained unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Archives containing parent traversal are rejected before any members are installed.
requirements.summary: The mixed traversal archive was rejected before incoming/ existed; protected/customer.txt remained unchanged. After restart, rejection was reconfirmed and the archive's otherwise-safe accepted.txt was still absent.

requirements.requirement: Archives containing symlink-based escapes are rejected before any members are installed.
requirements.summary: symlink.tar was rejected on its link member before incoming/ existed, and protected/customer.txt retained its original hash.

requirements.requirement: Preserve all supplied source packages and sibling protected files.
requirements.summary: Post-restart hashes for all four archives and protected/customer.txt match the preparation baseline; the final tree still contains them.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged before and after implementation and restart. The replacement ran successfully using the installed Python 2.4.3 runtime.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct behavior on the supplied normal and malformed archives. The independent restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, the reboot was acknowledged and observed through downtime, a different boot ID appeared, and safe rejection, normal extraction, data, OS, and kernel state were verified after recovery. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the reboot.
limitations: Behavior was directly tested against the four supplied archives, but there was no separate dynamic test of every generalized archive ordering or a pre-existing symlink placed within incoming/; confidence in those broader cases also relies on inspection of the captured implementation.

Systemd service-state collection was unsupported on this legacy host, and the lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum operation, so those snapshots cannot independently establish service or package-manager health.
The executor-caused /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log remained in the final lifecycle snapshot.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The final state is focused and clean apart from one reboot log. One unnecessary interim mutation occurred: cmd-65faae1a057c47af copied a syntactically invalid draft over bin/unpack after its compile invocation reported an error; it was subsequently replaced by the valid final implementation in cmd-f5e99dd3add94dd8. Temporary implementation and verification artifacts were then removed by cmd-14362db151d94ef6. The restart action in cmd-14734c18e2164f4d had a necessary protocol role, but its /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log residue remained after completion. No new sockets or demonstrated package-state degradation appeared.
